# Agent ↔ control-plane wire contract (gRPC)

This is the **third** API surface, and the only one that is not HTTP. It is
specified by protobuf IDL in `engine/proto/ebpfsoc/v1/`; the generated Go
stubs in `engine/gen/` are committed so consumers build without protoc.

Transport is gRPC over **mutual TLS**. The tenant identity of every call is
taken from the verified client certificate (`O=<tenant>`), never from the
message body — see the tenancy note in `common.proto`. An agent therefore
cannot assign itself a tenant, and a compromised payload cannot widen scope.

`make proto-lint` validates this IDL on every CI run.

## `command.proto`

> CommandService — control-plane → agent actions. The agent dials out and holds
> the stream (works through customer NAT with no inbound access); the CP pushes
> SIGNED commands down it. Every command is verified, acked, and audited on both
> ends, and local guardrails override any command. See docs/plan/wire-contract.md §5.

### service `CommandService`

- **`Commands`**(`stream CommandAck`) → `stream Command`
  - The agent opens the stream and sends CommandAcks; the server streams
  - Commands. Agent-initiated so no inbound connectivity to the host is needed.
### message `Command`

### enum `Plane`

Plane selects which enforcement plane a command acts on. The agent runs two
independent gateways — processes (cgroup/BPF, a sever is a SIGKILL) and LAN
devices (tc, a sever is a reversible drop rule) — and they arm separately.
UNSPECIFIED means the process plane so that an older control plane, which had
no plane field, keeps its existing meaning.

### message `SetMode`

### message `Jail`

Jail moves a target to a choke tier immediately (operator-driven override).

### message `Thaw`

### message `SetThresholds`

### message `ApplyPreset`

### message `KillSwitch`

KillSwitch is the fleet-wide emergency halt of enforcement (threat-model EN-2).

### message `UpdateProtectedList`

UpdateProtectedList adjusts the local allow-lists the agent refuses to enforce
against. NOTE: the agent applies conservative local minimums regardless — a
command can never remove sudo/sshd/systemd protection and cause self-lockout
(threat-model EN-1/EN-4; the sudo-lockout trap).

### message `CommandAck`

## `common.proto`

> Shared message types for the agent ↔ control-plane wire contract.
> See docs/plan/wire-contract.md for the full specification.
> 
> TENANCY INVARIANT: no message in this package carries an authoritative
> tenant_id. Tenant identity is derived from the mTLS client certificate at
> the ingest/command edge (docs/plan/tenant-isolation-invariant.md R1). This is
> deliberate — a payload tenant field could only ever be tamper-detection
> telemetry, never an authorization input.

### enum `EnforcementMode`

EnforcementMode mirrors the engine's boot/runtime mode. Boot mode comes only
from -enforce today; making it explicit on the wire lets the control plane
observe and (via the command channel) request mode changes, while the agent
retains local authority (docs/plan/threat-model.md EN-5).

### message `AgentInfo`

AgentInfo is the agent's self-report of identity and capabilities. Carries NO
tenant_id (see the tenancy invariant above); agent_id is authoritative only
as derived from the client cert — the copy here is for display/telemetry.

### message `DataPlaneState`

DataPlaneState reports both choke data planes so the fleet service can render
real enforcement posture (architecture.md §3.5 agent registry).

### message `KernelPolicy`

KernelPolicy is one Tetragon TracingPolicy as the KERNEL currently has it —
not as a config file describes it. The distinction matters: a policy edited on
disk but never reloaded still runs its old version, and a policy deleted at
runtime returns on the next restart if its file remains.

### message `ProcessEvent`

ProcessEvent mirrors internal/store.Event (process_exec / process_kprobe).

### message `Alert`

Alert mirrors internal/store.Alert (a scored suspicious chain).

### message `Decision`

Decision mirrors internal/store.Decision — an entry of the hash-chained
enforcement audit (internal/store/decisions.go). Every field that feeds the
chain hash is carried VERBATIM so the central mirror re-verifies the
tamper-evident chain per tenant without trusting the server or transport
ordering (docs/plan/tenant-isolation-invariant.md Layer 3). The audit chain
itself is never modified by this contract.

The chain hash is sha256(prev_hash || 0x00 || canonical), where `canonical`
(decisions.go) is built from: id, occurred_at, action, from_state→to_state,
exec_id, pid, score, dry_run. Those fields are therefore load-bearing for
re-verification; prev_hash/hash are hex strings exactly as stored.

## `enrollment.proto`

> EnrollmentService — the one channel reachable with server-auth TLS + a
> one-time bootstrap token. It exists solely to issue the mTLS client cert that
> every other channel requires. See docs/plan/wire-contract.md §3.

### service `EnrollmentService`

- **`Enroll`**(`EnrollRequest`) → `EnrollResponse`
  - Enroll exchanges a one-time, tenant-scoped bootstrap token + a CSR for a
  - client certificate whose subject encodes tenant_id + agent_id. Idempotent
  - only in that a spent token is rejected (threat-model SC-7).
- **`Renew`**(`RenewRequest`) → `EnrollResponse`
  - Renew re-issues a certificate for an ALREADY-enrolled agent, called over
  - its existing mTLS identity — no bootstrap token. The tenant_id + agent_id
  - are read from the caller's verified client certificate, never the request,
  - so an agent cannot change tenants at renewal (isolation invariant R4). This
  - lets a long-lived agent rotate before expiry without an operator minting a
  - fresh token (threat-model CH-6).
### message `RenewRequest`

### message `EnrollRequest`

### message `EnrollResponse`

## `heartbeat.proto`

> HeartbeatService — periodic agent health/liveness + hints. Cheap and
> unary; the authoritative agent registry (architecture.md §3.5) is built from
> these. A missed heartbeat never stops enforcement (autonomy invariant).
> See docs/plan/wire-contract.md §2.

### service `HeartbeatService`

- **`Heartbeat`**(`HeartbeatRequest`) → `HeartbeatResponse`
### message `HeartbeatRequest`

### message `BucketSummary`

BucketSummary is one kernel token bucket — the per-PID rate limit the choke
gateway actually installed. It is the evidence that a throttle reached the
kernel rather than only being recorded as a decision.

### message `CgroupSummary`

CgroupSummary is one choke tier and the PIDs the kernel reports inside it.
The console renders it as the cgroup map: which processes are actually
confined right now, as opposed to which ones a decision row claims are.

### message `ProcessSummary`

ProcessSummary is one live host process, joined with its choke state where
the gateway is tracking it. Powers the console's process picker, which on the
control plane had nothing to pick from.

### message `ChokeSummary`

ChokeSummary is one process the agent is currently choking (or watching),
trimmed to what an operator scans in a fleet-wide view.

### message `DeviceSummary`

DeviceSummary is one device under the MAC gateway (empty when the device
data plane is inactive).

### message `HeartbeatResponse`

## `policy.proto`

> PolicyService — the agent pulls SIGNED policy bundles (TracingPolicies +
> ChokePolicy DSL + thresholds + protected lists) and verifies the signature
> before applying. Local files remain bootstrap/fallback. The agent keeps
> enforcing its last-applied bundle if the control plane is unreachable
> (autonomy invariant). See docs/plan/wire-contract.md §5-6.

### service `PolicyService`

- **`GetBundle`**(`PolicyPullRequest`) → `PolicyBundle`
  - Agent presents its current etag; the server returns a new signed bundle or
  - not_modified. Verify-before-apply (threat-model SC-4).
### message `PolicyPullRequest`

### message `PolicyBundle`

## `telemetry.proto`

> TelemetryService — the agent → control-plane firehose (events, alerts,
> decisions). At-least-once with agent-assigned dedup keys and WAL-backed
> resume so reconnects never double-count or lose data.
> See docs/plan/wire-contract.md §4.

### service `TelemetryService`

- **`StreamTelemetry`**(`stream TelemetryBatch`) → `stream TelemetryAck`
  - Bidirectional: the agent streams batches; the server streams cumulative
  - acks and optional backpressure. The agent resumes from the last acked
  - sequence held in its local WAL after any partition.

### message `TelemetryRecord`

### message `TelemetryAck`
